blocks: Entry requirements: This information is for people travelling on a full ‘British citizen’ passport from the UK. It is based on the UK government’s understanding of the current rules for the most common types of travel.
Entry requirements: The authorities in Kenya set and enforce entry rules. If you’re not sure how these requirements apply to you, contact the Kenyan High Commission in the UK.
Passport validity requirements: To enter Kenya, your passport must have an ‘expiry date’ at least 6 months after the date you arrive and at least 2 blank pages.
Passport validity requirements: Check with your travel provider that your passport and other travel documents meet requirements. Renew your passport if you need to.
Passport validity requirements: You will be denied entry if you do not have a valid travel document or try to use a passport that has been reported lost or stolen.
Dual nationals: When returning to the UK, British citizens must carry a valid British passport or certificate of entitlement. See Dual citizenship.
Visa requirements: You must apply online for electronic travel authorisation in advance of travel. The local authorities recommend applying at least 2 weeks before your departure.
Visa requirements: Travellers who currently hold a visa can continue to travel using their visa until it expires.
Visa requirements: For information on work permits and residency, check the Kenyan Department of Immigration requirements.
Mandatory travel insurance: From 5 October 2026, most travellers visiting Kenya for less than 12 months must have Kenyan Government-provided travel health insurance.

Mandatory travel insurance: If you require an Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA), you must buy this insurance as part of the application process. If you already hold a valid eTA, you must obtain the insurance through the Kenyan eCitizen insurance portal. Foreign travel insurance policies are not accepted in place of this requirement.
Mandatory travel insurance: The insurance is valid for 90 days and can be used for multiple entries into Kenya during that period.

Mandatory travel insurance: The requirement does not apply to Kenyan citizens, holders of valid Kenyan residence status, citizens of East African Community partner states, or transit passengers that are not passing through Kenyan immigration control.
Mandatory travel insurance: You should also make sure you have travel insurance that covers your individual needs.
Vaccine requirements: To enter Kenya, you must have a certificate to prove you’ve had a yellow fever vaccination if you’re coming from a country listed as a transmission risk.
Vaccine requirements: For full details about medical entry requirements and recommended vaccinations, see TravelHealthPro’s Kenya guide.

Ebola screening: Travellers arriving in Kenya, particularly those coming from Uganda, Ethiopia and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), may be subject to enhanced health screening measures due to the ongoing Ebola outbreak centred in the DRC. The World Health Organisation (WHO) has declared this a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.
Customs rules: There are strict rules about goods you can take into or out of Kenya. You must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.

Taking drones into Kenya: It is illegal to import or export drones without prior approval from the Kenya Civil Aviation Authority (KCAA). Contact the KCAA well in advance of travel if you wish to bring a drone to Kenya.
